title: Natural linear comparison of equivariant coequalizer presentations
statement:
Let $\mathcal D$ be a monoidal category [def-sfb-monoidal-category], $A$ a monoid object [sk-def-sfb-ring-object], and $J$ a category. Write $U:\operatorname{Mod}_A(\mathcal D)\to\mathcal D$ for the forgetful functor [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Let $H:J\to\mathcal D$ and $B,P,Q:J\to\operatorname{Mod}_A(\mathcal D)$ be functors, and let $a,b:H\Rightarrow U\circ B$ be natural transformations. Suppose $q:U\circ B\Rightarrow U\circ P$ and $r:U\circ B\Rightarrow U\circ Q$ are natural transformations such that, for every $j\in J$:
(1) $q_j:B_j\to P_j$ and $r_j:B_j\to Q_j$ are coequalizers of $a_j,b_j$ in $\mathcal D$; explicitly $q_ja_j=q_jb_j$, and every $h:B_j\to T$ equalizing $a_j,b_j$ factors uniquely as $h=kq_j$, and likewise for $r_j$;
(2) writing $\beta_j,\delta^P_j,\delta^Q_j$ for the $A$-actions, one has
\[
q_j\circ\beta_j=\delta^P_j\circ(1_A\otimes q_j),\qquad r_j\circ\beta_j=\delta^Q_j\circ(1_A\otimes r_j);
\]
(3) $A\otimes-$ preserves these coequalizers, meaning $1_A\otimes q_j$ and $1_A\otimes r_j$ are coequalizers of $1_A\otimes a_j,1_A\otimes b_j$.
There is a unique natural isomorphism $c:Q\xrightarrow{\sim}P$ of $A$-module-valued functors whose underlying components satisfy $c_j\circ r_j=q_j$. Its inverse $d:P\xrightarrow{\sim}Q$ satisfies $d_j\circ q_j=r_j$. In particular,
\[
c_j\delta^Q_j=\delta^P_j(1_A\otimes c_j),\quad d_j\delta^P_j=\delta^Q_j(1_A\otimes d_j),\quad P(u)c_j=c_kQ(u)
\]
for every $u:j\to k$ in $J$, and $d_jc_j=1_{Q_j}$, $c_jd_j=1_{P_j}$. No colimit indexed by $J$, smallness of $J$, or module structure on $H_j$ is required.
